                                   5                        IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                                   6                    FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA
                                   7
                                   8     BAYERISCHE MOTOREN WERKE                      Case No. 26-cv-05274-CRB
                                         AG,
                                   9
                                                      Plaintiff,                       ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR
                                  10                                                   A TEMPORARY RESTRAINING
                                                v.                                     ORDER
                                  11
                                         ZYNC INC.,
                                  12
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                                      Defendant.
                                  13
                                             Bayerische Motoren Werke Aktiengesellschaft (“BMW”) sues to enforce a forum
                                  14
                                       selection clause against Zync Inc. (“Zync”). Compl. (dkt. 1). Zync and BMW of North
                                  15
                                       America, LLC (“BMW NA”), BMW’s subsidiary, initially entered into a Pilot Project
                                  16
                                       Agreement (“PPA”) for in-vehicle infotainment technology. Id. ¶ 18. That agreement was
                                  17
                                       subject to the terms of BMW’s and Zync’s prior confidentiality agreement (“NDA”),
                                  18
                                       which contained a forum selection clause and choice-of-law provision. Id. ¶ 21. Those
                                  19
                                       terms state that the agreement “shall be governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of
                                  20
                                       Germany and the exclusive place of jurisdiction shall be Munich, unless a different place
                                  21
                                       of jurisdiction is required by mandatory law.” Id.
                                  22
                                             Eventually, the partnership soured and Zync sued BMW NA in state court on April
                                  23
                                       14, 2025, claiming that BMW NA misappropriated its trade secrets. Compl. ¶ 25. BMW
                                  24
                                       NA moved to dismiss the action based on the NDA’s forum selection clause. Id. ¶ 26.
                                  25
                                       Before the state court reached a decision on BMW NA’s motion to dismiss, Zync filed a
                                  26
                                       complaint against BMW and BMW NA with the International Trade Commission (“ITC”)
                                  27
                                       on February 23, 2026, premised on the same theory as the state action. Id. ¶ 28. On May
                                  28
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB          Document 29        Filed 06/12/26    Page 2 of 4




                                   1   12, 2026, the state court granted BMW NA’s motion and dismissed the case on forum
                                   2   selection grounds. Id. ¶ 29. The ITC proceedings are ongoing.
                                   3          BMW moved for a temporary restraining order (“TRO”) enjoining Zync from
                                   4   participating in the ITC action until the Court can resolve BMW’s preliminary injunction
                                   5   motion. Mot. (dkt. 10). Zync opposes. Opp’n (dkt. 19). The Court GRANTS BMW’s
                                   6   motion and enjoins Zync from participating in the ITC action for 14 days. The Court will
                                   7   hear argument on BMW’s motion for a preliminary injunction on June 22, 2026.
                                   8   I.     LEGAL STANDARD
                                   9          A party seeking a TRO must establish: (1) a likelihood of success on the merits; (2)
                                  10   a likelihood of irreparable harm absent preliminary relief; (3) that the balance of equities
                                  11   tips in the plaintiff’s favor; and (4) that an injunction is in the public interest. Winter v.
                                  12   Nat. Res. Def. Council, Inc., 555 U.S. 7, 20 (2008). The “[l]ikelihood of success on the
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   merits ‘is the most important Winter factor.’” Disney Enters., Inc. v. VidAngel, Inc., 869
                                  14   F.3d 848, 856 (9th Cir. 2017) (quoting Garcia v. Google, Inc., 786 F.3d 733, 740 (9th Cir.
                                  15   2015)).
                                  16   II.    DISCUSSION
                                  17          The Court finds that all Winter factors have been met here. Each factor is examined
                                  18   in turn.
                                  19          A.     Likelihood of Success on the Merits
                                  20          Just like the state court, this Court concludes that the NDA’s forum selection clause
                                  21   is valid and applicable to the ITC action. See Dkt. 1-3 (“If Zync wishes to pursue this
                                  22   litigation, it must do so in Munich, Germany.”). “A forum selection clause is
                                  23   presumptively valid.” M/S Bremen v. Zapata Off-Shore Co., 407 U.S. 1, 15 (1972). The
                                  24   NDA explicitly applies “to all and any confidential information, including Trade Secrets,
                                  25   directly or indirectly disclosed by a Party or a Connected Company of a Party in
                                  26   connection with the Project.” NDA (dkt. 1-1) at 2. Zync’s ITC complaint plainly arises
                                  27   out of confidential information and trade secrets BMW purportedly stole for itself. See
                                  28   Dkt. 1-6. Indeed, Zync admitted that the ITC action overlapped with the state court case—
                                                                                       2
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB         Document 29        Filed 06/12/26   Page 3 of 4




                                   1   which was dismissed based on the forum selection clause—and asserted “the same trade
                                   2   secret misappropriation allegations and nearly the same tortious interference allegations.”
                                   3   Dkt. 10-4.
                                   4          Consequently, the Court finds that BMW has established a likelihood of success on
                                   5   the merits.
                                   6          B.     Irreparable Harm
                                   7          “Courts around the country regularly hold that the ‘depriv[ation] of [a] bargained-
                                   8   for choice of forum’ constitutes irreparable harm sufficient to support an injunction.”
                                   9   Google, 2025 WL 964692 at *11 (quoting Nippon Shinyaku Co. v. Sarepta Therapeutics,
                                  10   Inc., 25 F.4th 998, 1008 (Fed. Cir. 2022)). And “an ITC proceeding can have a direct and
                                  11   significant impact on a responding party.” General Protecht Group, 651 F.3d at 1364
                                  12   (emphasis in original) (affirming finding of irreparable harm where a party was litigating
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   before the ITC and other courts despite a forum selection clause). Accordingly, the Court
                                  14   finds that BMW has shown irreparable harm.
                                  15          C.     Balance of the Equities
                                  16          The balance of the equities tips in BMW’s favor. As discussed, BMW would face
                                  17   hardship by being deprived of its forum selection clause and litigating in multiple forums.
                                  18   Moreover, “[h]aving contracted for a specific forum, [Zync] should not be heard to argue
                                  19   that the enforcement of the contract into which it freely entered would cause hardship.”
                                  20   General Protecht Group, 651 F.3d at 1365. And Zync has not demonstrated that it would
                                  21   not get substantially similar relief in Germany.
                                  22          D.     Public Interest
                                  23          The public interest factor also weighs in BMW’s favor. “Public policy strongly
                                  24   favors the enforcement of forum selection clauses.” Koken v. Stateco Inc., No. C 05-
                                  25   03007 JF, 2006 WL 2918050, at *8 (N.D. Cal. Oct. 11, 2006).
                                  26   III.   CONCLUSION
                                  27          For the foregoing reasons, the Court GRANTS BMW’s motion for a temporary
                                  28   restraining order. Nothing in this order is to be construed as limiting the ITC’s
                                                                                     3
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB       Document 29       Filed 06/12/26   Page 4 of 4




                                   1   management over the action before it or its ability to resolve motions—like BMW’s
                                   2   termination motion—that are already pending. BMW is ordered to pay a bond of $1,000
                                   3   pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 65(c).
                                   4         IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                   5         Dated: June 12, 2026
                                                                                       CHARLES R. BREYER
                                   6                                                   United States District Judge
